hero.title: Tell Photoshop what you want.
hero.lead: Photoshop MCP connects Claude, Cursor and any MCP client to Adobe Photoshop. Remove backgrounds, retouch, color grade, batch export — from a chat, in one undo step.
hero.trust: Free and open source (MIT). Runs on macOS and Windows with Photoshop 2012 through 2025.

demo.prompt: Remove the background from this portrait and export a 1080×1350 Instagram version.

install.fallback: If the button does nothing, paste this into your config instead
install.verifyPrompt: Ping Photoshop and list open documents.
install.verifyExpect: You should see the Photoshop version and the names of any open documents.
install.mcpbNote: The .mcpb bundle is attached to every GitHub release.

works.title: Works with the tools you already use
works.more: and any client that runs local MCP servers

steps.title: Install
steps.text: One click in your client, or one command. The server runs on your own machine.

steps.title: Open Photoshop
steps.text: Any version from 2012 on. Nothing to load inside Photoshop — the server talks to it directly.

steps.title: Type a prompt
steps.text: Ask in plain language. The assistant reads the document, does the steps, and shows you a preview.

recipes.title: What you can ask for
recipes.lead: Sixteen ready-made workflows. Each one runs as a single undo step, so nothing is ever left half-done.

ide.title: Inside your editor or assistant
ide.text: Add the MCP server to Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code or any other client. Your assistant gets {n} Photoshop tools and picks the right ones for each request.

ui.title: In the standalone Web UI
ui.text: No editor needed. One command starts a local chat that drives Photoshop. Bring an API key for Claude, GPT, Gemini or OpenRouter, or reuse your Claude Code account.
ui.caption: Action Plan mode: one planning call, then every step runs in sequence.

agents.title: Built for agents, not one-off scripts
agents.lead: Raw scripting from a language model is brittle: it guesses at layer types, wastes tokens on retries, and one failed step leaves the document in an unknown state. The server fixes that at the protocol level.

items.title: State before action
items.text: get_state, get_preview and get_capabilities tell the assistant what is open, what layer is active and which features this Photoshop version supports.

items.title: Recipes are one undo step
items.text: Multi-step outcomes are wrapped in a single history state. Undo once and the whole recipe is gone.

items.title: Errors that say what to try next
items.text: Failures come back as structured JSON with a code and a suggested_next_tool, so the assistant can recover instead of guessing.

items.title: Action Plan
items.text: In the Web UI, one planning call produces the full list of steps, which then run without a model round-trip in between.

items.title: Generative AI and Neural Filters
items.text: Firefly generative fill, remove, expand and upscale; sky replacement; and Neural Filters through an optional UXP bridge.

items.title: macOS and Windows
items.text: AppleScript on macOS, COM on Windows. Photoshop is auto-detected, including multiple installed versions.

toolsTeaser.title: {n} tools, all searchable
toolsTeaser.lead: {atomic} atomic tools for precise edits plus {recipes} recipes for whole outcomes — documents, layers, masks, filters, color, text, export, generative AI.

items.q: Is this an official Adobe product?
items.a: No. Photoshop MCP is an independent, community-maintained open-source project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Adobe. Photoshop is a trademark of Adobe Inc.

items.q: Do I need an API key?
items.a: Not for the MCP server itself — it runs locally. Your client (Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code…) already talks to a model. The standalone Web UI needs either a provider API key or a Claude Code account.

Photoshop 2012 through 2025 on macOS and Windows. Some tools need newer versions: Select Subject needs 23+, WebP/AVIF export needs 23.2+, generative tools need a Firefly-enabled Photoshop and an Adobe account with credits.
Only the generative tools (fill, remove, expand, upscale, sky replacement, image generation) do, and only when you ask for them. Everything else is regular Photoshop automation.

Photoshop commands run on your machine. Your images never leave it unless your own model provider receives a preview you asked for. The server sends anonymous usage events by default; set ANALYTICS_DISABLED=1 to turn them off.

items.q: Why can't I use it from ChatGPT or claude.ai in the browser?
items.a: Browser assistants only accept remote connectors, and Photoshop lives on your computer. Use a desktop client, or the Web UI, which runs locally.

cta.title: Open Photoshop. Start typing.
cta.lead: Install takes a minute. The first prompt takes ten seconds.
